issues.legal_issue: An individual is resident under the statutory dwelling-place test only if the individual is present in the taxable territories for some time during the relevant year and maintains, or has a dwelling place maintained for them, as their home for the required period.
material_facts: The individual was born, brought up, and conducted business in Ceylon, where the individual also had properties and family.
The individual visited India only occasionally and stayed variously at a family house, a lodging house, and hotels.
The family house was managed and maintained by another family member for the other family members; the individual did not enjoy family income or participate in managing the family properties.
Although the individual had an interest in the family house and a right to occupy it, the evidence showed that the individual stayed there as a guest and that it was not the individual's home.
The individual was present in the taxable territories for some time during the relevant years.
issues.conclusion: The individual was a non-resident because the family house was not maintained at the individual's instance or for the individual's benefit as a home.
issues.legal_principle: Section 4A(a)(ii) of the Indian Income Tax Act, 1922, creates a statutory test of territorial connection applicable irrespective of personal law. It requires both some presence in the taxable territories during the year and a dwelling place maintained there for the required period by the individual or for the individual's benefit. A dwelling place must be an abode or home, not merely a house the individual may occupy; maintenance by another must be at the individual's instance, behest, or request and for the individual's benefit. Mere fractional ownership and a right to occupy a family house are insufficient. The Court approved C.I.T., Bombay North v. Foolabhai Khodabhai Patel and Pickles v. Foulsham, approved C.I.T., Madras v. Janab A. P. Mohamed Noohu, and distinguished S. M. Zackariah Sahib v. C.I.T., Madras and Ramjibhai Hansibhai Patel v. Income Tax Officer.

predicates.individual_tax_residence_determination: The proceeding determines whether an individual meets a statutory test for residence in a territory for tax purposes.
predicates.present_in_territory_during_year: The individual was present in the territory for some time during the relevant year.
predicates.dwelling_maintained_for_individual_as_ho: A dwelling was maintained for the required period at the individual's instance or for the individual's benefit as the individual's abode or home.

issues.definition: In an individual tax-residence determination, the individual is non-resident if they were not present in the territory during the year or no dwelling was maintained for them there as their home for the required period.

issues.legal_issue: Penalties for late filing of returns cannot stand when the assessments are cancelled on the ground that the taxpayer was a non-resident.
material_facts: Penalties were levied for failure to file returns on time.
The Tribunal upheld the finding that the individual was a non-resident and cancelled the assessments and, as a consequence, the penalties.
The High Court answered the referred penalty question in favour of the individual, and the Supreme Court dismissed the Revenue's appeals.
issues.conclusion: The cancellation of the penalties was upheld as a consequence of the cancellation of the assessments.
issues.legal_principle: The Tribunal cancelled the penalties under section 28(1)(a) of the Indian Income Tax Act, 1922, as a consequence of cancelling the assessments after finding the individual to be a non-resident. The Supreme Court dismissed the appeals and left that result undisturbed; it gave no separate analysis of the penalty provision or reliance on earlier cases for this issue.

predicates.late_return_penalty_proceeding: The proceeding concerns penalties imposed on a taxpayer for filing returns late.
predicates.assessments_cancelled_after_taxpayer_fou: The assessments were cancelled after the taxpayer was found not to be resident under the applicable tax-residence test.

issues.definition: In a proceeding concerning penalties for late returns, if the assessments are cancelled after the taxpayer is found to be non-resident, the late-return penalties are cancelled.
